• Simple by default

Because caring for someone shouldn’t feel overwhelming—and technology should help, not hinder.

Brain-Based Hearing CareTM (BBHCTM) is a proprietary, the world's first brain-centered framework redefining the future of hearing care through neuroscience, clinical insight, and engineering integration.

BBHCTM is founded on a simple but transformative principle: hearing is not an ear-level event — it is a brain function. Meaningful hearing care must therefore align with neural processing, cognitive load, predictive perception, and real-world listening demands, not amplification alone.

Developed across fourteen comprehensive volumes, BBHCTM unites neuro-audiology, oto-neurology, auditory cognition, vestibular integration, and hearing technology into a single, modular, neurofunctional ecosystem. The framework guides how hearing care is designed, evaluated, and delivered, supporting precision interventions that reduce listening effort, enhance speech clarity, preserve spatial awareness, and restore perceptual trust.

BBHCTM is not a product, algorithm, or device brand. It is a foundational architecture for brain-aligned hearing care — providing clinicians, engineers, researchers, and innovators with shared principles, methodologies, and language to advance the next era of hearing science and engineering.

The mission of BBHCTM is to move hearing care beyond sound delivery and toward rebuilding the listening brain, one patient, one clinician, and one innovation at a time.

Description:
توی چند سال اخیر، مهاجرت دغدغهی بخش بزرگی از جامعهی ایران شده. اگه قبلا، مهاجرت تحصیلی در سنین 20 تا 30 سالگی بخش عمدهی مهاجرتها رو تشکیل میداد، اما این روزها تقریبا همهی گروههای جامعهی ایران درگیر این قضیه شده.
از طرفی خیلی از کسانی که میخوان مهاجرت کنن، نگاهشون به مهاجرت معمولا از دریچهی تصاویر و فیلمهاییه که مهاجران قبلی در اینستاگرام و سایر شبکههای اجتماعی منتشر میکنن که لزوما همهی واقعیت رو نشون نمیده.
من 4-5 ماه پیش شروع کردم به صحبت با ایرانیان مهاجری که در بخشهای مختلف دنیا زندگی میکنن تا از تجربههای روزمرهی زندگیشون و واقعیتهایی که هر روز باهاش مواجه هستن بگن و این گفتوگوها رو در پادکست «آن سوی خط» منتشر میکنم.
خوشحال میشم این گفتوگوها رو بشنوید و نظرتون رو در مورد مطالبی که منتشر میکنم باهام به اشتراک بذارید. اگر هم مهاجرت کرده اید و علاقمندید که تجربیاتتون از زندگی روزمره بعد از مهاجرت رو با دیگران هم به اشتراک بذارید، خوشحال میشم بهم پیام بدید و با هم قرار گفتوگو بذاریم.

In the recent years, because of the economic and social situation in Iran, a lot of people are thinking about immigrating to other countries in search of a better life. In the past, most of those Iranian immigrants were in their 20-30s and were immigrating for studying in another country, but these days, we are seeing people of almost all ages are looking for immigration.
But the way they learn about other countries is through the images that previous immigrants posting on Facebook, Instagram, and other social networks, which we all know it's not showing the whole picture!

About 4-5 months ago, I've started speaking with Iranian immigrants all over the world and sharing their experiences from day-to-day life, and created a podcast to share those experiences with others too.

L’entreprise à vocation sociale UTAPI Consultants est une initiative autochtone, qui s'inspire des pratiques d'autochtonisation et de décolonisation qui se font au Canada. Elle a été créée par Joannie Gill, Pekuakamiushkueu, une femme de la Nation ilnu, qui a pour but de rassembler des personnes clées qui contribueront par leurs forces complémentaires, à un monde plus juste et équitable envers les Premiers peuples.

Mission
Notre mission est de soutenir un processus de décolonisation bienveillante dans la population francophone en accompagnant les changements auprès des individus, gestionnaires, étudiants, enseignants et des professionnel.le.s, allié.e.s aux causes et droits des Premiers Peuples. 

Valeurs et vision
Par la Collaboration, l'Humilité, la Bienveillance, l'Intuitivité, ainsi que le Dynamisme, nous souhaitons créer des espaces et des environnements propices à la réappropriation identitaire des personnes autochtones dans leur processus de guérison.

Que veut dire UTAPI ?
Le mot UTAPI se traduit de l'ilnu-aimun (la langue ilnu) vers le mot RACINE. Ce mot détient le symbole puissant de la fierté de notre identité culturelle.

Name: Sports Industry Credit Association  (SICA)
Description:

The Sports Industry Credit Association (SICA) was founded in 1980 by sporting goods, ski and outdoor manufacturers and importers. Their goal was to assemble a network of like suppliers that would work together in exchanging credit information and would also intervene on their behalf in the face of unforeseen difficulties, bankruptcies and retailer re-organization, so that the sport/ski/outdoor industry would have a common voice to deal with insolvency and credit issues in the sporting goods industry.

Fast forward 40 years later, we have expanded our services to the US region. Located in Burlington, Vermont, SICA-US will focus on its level of service to its 500+ Brand Members while remaining true to its purpose of providing a confidential environment for members to exchange credit information. Today, SICA-US is considered one of the premiere credit organizations in the US with a constantly growing membership base across North America.

In addition to representing the vast majority of the US Ski and Snowboard Outdoor Industry, SICA-US has launched into other sporting goods segments, including bike, golf, footwear, and team.

SICA-US is constantly evolving to improve the quality of its information base. For more information please visit, www.sica-us.com or call 1-855-437-8846.

Description:
Since 2012, Claris Healthcare has been enabling patients to manage their own care at home. Our care platform is used across the remote care continuum including social, chronic, and rehabilitation.   

Our Remote Patient Monitoring (Claris Continuum), Social Isolation (Claris Companion) and Acute Rehabilitation (Claris reflex) configurations require no on-site installation, setup or training - they work right out of the box.

Providers use Claris Continuum to engage and monitor patients with chronic diseases such as heart disease, diabetes, COPD, etc.  The sophisticated caregiver portal simplifies recording of activities for RPM billings, helping to maximize revenues.

Family members use Claris Companion to communicate  with and monitor their aging loved-ones remotely.  Companion is designed to be accessible to even the most techno-phobic users and can be deployed into the homes of seniors without the need for installation, setup or training. 

Providers use Claris Reflex to guide patients through rehabilitation after acute interventions - providing timely advice and coaching in the home using customized Care Programs.  Patients report better overall satisfaction due to simpler communication with care providers, access to instructional videos and information, as well as direct feedback on their recovery performance. 

The Claris platform offers a wide range of deployment options - from fully integrated kits provided by Claris through 'bring your own device' for those who have their own smart phones or tablets, through 'direct to cloud' vital signs devices that require no mobile device in the home at all.  Providers can choose any mixture of device options for their patients, all reporting back to one common care portal. 

The Claris platform is all about flexibility, configurability, accessibility and engagement.  No other home care delivery platform provides such a wide range of options in one product.

ما متعهد هستیم که به شرکتها کمک کنیم تا فناوریهای جدید فوتونیک خود را با عمل کردن به عنوان یک مرکز بین صنعت و دانشگاه به بازار عرضه کنند. به منظور تسهیل در توسعه فناوریهای جدید اپتیک و فوتونیک، شرکتهایی از صنایع بهداشت، غذا، حملونقل و اتصالات پرسرعت و همچنین دانشگاهها را گرد هم آوردهایم تا به عنوان پل ارتباطی بین این شرکتها و دانشگاهها عمل کنیم.
علاوهبراین، ما میزبان بحث و گفتگو با این شرکتها هستیم تا به آنها کمک کنیم با این فناوریهای پیشرفته به پتانسیل کامل خود دست یابند. ما همچنین بهعنوان واسطهای بین دانشگاه و صنعت عمل میکنیم و به آنها کمک میکنیم تا به همكاري مشتركي دست پيدا كنند. ما اطلاعاتی در مورد کنفرانسها، انجمنها و نمایشگاهها در اختیار اعضای خود قرار میدهیم.

The photonicSpots will provide members with news and information about annual events, conferences, exhibits, forums and even career development and training opportunities.

Description: Le Conseil de presse du Québec est un organisme privé, à but non lucratif, qui œuvre depuis plus de 50 ans à la protection de la liberté de la presse et à la défense du droit du public à une information de qualité. Son action s’étend à tous les médias d’information distribués ou diffusés au Québec, qu’ils soient membres ou non du Conseil, qu’ils appartiennent à la presse écrite ou électronique. Le Conseil reçoit les plaintes du public et rend des décisions relativement à la déontologie journalistique. Mécanisme d’autorégulation de la presse, le Conseil ne peut être assimilé à un tribunal civil, il ne possède aucun pouvoir judiciaire, réglementaire, législatif ou coercitif; il n’impose aucune autre sanction que morale.

Sun Tzu said, "For to win one hundred victories in one hundred battles is not the acme of skill. To subdue the enemy without fighting is the acme of skill."

When rules are updated new problems arise and clarification and education is required. Now more than ever timely information is needed to succeed and prevent problems before they occur.

Trade Services Update is the only journal and searchable on-line database in the world devoted to the topic of Trade Services. Our purpose is to share knowledge gained from practical experience. Our Editors are comprised of top professionals from around the globe who handle documentary credits, standby letters of credit, bank guarantees, documentary collections, and surrounding legal issues on a daily basis and feel the pulse of the trading world. By reading the publication you will learn from their experience, case studies and creative problem solving techniques. Name: Independent First Nations
Description:
Prior to the mid-1960s, most First Nations communities in Ontario were independent of each other.  One exception was the Union of Ontario Indians. It was incorporated in 1949 and represents 39 First Nations.

The Association of Iroquois and Allied Indians (AIAI) was established as a non-profit organization in 1969 and represents 8 First Nations.

In 1973, more than 45 First Nation communities of Treaty No. 9 created an umbrella organization called the Grand Council of Treaty No. 9.  Since 1983, it is known as the Nishnawbe Aski Nation.

In the 60s and 70s, many First Nations were establishing collective organizations. The only community not to join an organization was Bear Island. Bear Island along with Six Nations of the Grand River would become the initial participants as the Independent First Nations. They would be joined by the Mohawk Council of Akwesasne. Since then, a growing number of First Nations have chosen to leave existing Provincial/Territorial Organizations (PTOs) to join the Independent First Nations. 

In 1999, the Independent First Nations held a Retreat to achieve unity and to identify areas where they could work closer together. At that session, the Independent First Nations Protocol was introduced. It established the relationship amongst the Independent First Nations built around five principles:

- Respect and truth;
- Open communication;
- Working constructively on issues of mutual concern;
- Acknowledging the autonomy of each Independent First Nation; and
- Using the expertise within each Independent First Nation cooperatively.

The IFN Protocol established its purpose in working together: where possible, to unify on matters important to them; to jointly access funding holistically, and to combine their expertise to benefit all.

Since then, the IFN has been working to implement the protocol in practical ways and prioritizing issues and areas that the IFNs can work together on for their mutual benefit.

Name: Check-Out Planning Services Ltd.
Description:
From Loss, Comes A New Beginning
Who hasn’t experienced a sudden death in the family? It’s pure trauma made worse by the harsh decisions to follow, but does it really have to be that way?
As an only child with three adult children of her own, the daughter had instantly inherited the many complexities that await the loved ones of a family member who passes without an end-of-life plan. It had seemed like the mother would live forever, but a Sunday morning phone call utterly destroyed that notion.
As the reality of this sudden passing took hold, the daughter was left to wonder, what would her mother’s wishes have been? What would have mattered to her most? What would she have wanted? Although they had all been close, the grieving family was at a loss. The daughter’s grief took a backseat to the financial, moral and legal decisions that had to be made over the weeks and months that followed. Even the lesser items required a final decision such as... Who would inherit the TV that had been recently purchased?
Decisions such as cremation versus burial, autopsy or no, government requirements, tracking down all manner of service providers, pension and legal needs were cruel but necessary. The rapid distribution of the lifetime of possessions in her apartment, and calling family and friends with the painful news of the mother’s passing were distractions from the painful reality that after-all her mother was... Gone.
It became clear that there had to be a better way! Experiencing the death of a loved one is painful enough, but the myriad of decisions to be made could be much easier for those left behind. If only families had some guidance—a true sense of their loved one’s wishes and treasured memories. As a result, Check-Out was born.

Name: Data Scraping
Description:
1) Data scraping
Data scraping is the process of gathering essential information from a social media or website into a spreadsheet. Data scraping is one of the most effective ways to get data from a website.

2) Data extraction
The act of retrieving or processing data from a data source for data storage is called data extraction. Import into an intermediate extraction system is usually followed by data transformation and possibly the addition of metadata before export to another stage in the data workflow.

3) Web Scraping
Web scraping, also known as data scraping, is the process of importing data from a website into a spreadsheet. It is one of the most efficient ways to get data from the web, and in some cases channel that data to other websites.

4) Linkedin Scraping
LinkedIn scraping is just like web scraping. Here we create a filter according to the customer's requirement and scrape the data from that filter. Customer needs are usually based on specific company, job title, experience, geography etc.

5) Lead Generation
In marketing, lead generation is the initiation of consumer interest or inquiry about a business's product or service. A lead is a complete piece of information the customer wants. which may include name, address, contact details, current employment company name, company address, etc.

6) Cold email
A cold email is an unsolicited e-mail that is sent to a receiver without prior contact. It could also be defined as the email equivalent of cold calling. Cold emailing is a subset of email marketing and differs from transactional and warm emailing. Cold email, according to its proponents, is not spam.

7) Bulk Email Verification
We have our own made accurate and fast email checker. Our professional email verifier tools check every email at multiple levels with accuracy. We strive to make every customer smile.

Name: Canadian Cyber Threat Exchange (CCTX)
Description:
An independent, not-for-profit organization, the Canadian Cyber Threat Exchange (CCTX) is a private-sector initiative that supports the sharing and analytics of cyber threat information across sectors and with other sharing hubs, to help protect Canadian businesses, government and consumers, and strengthen Canada's economic prosperity.

SHARED INFORMATION MAKES US STRONGER

The CCTX’s mission is to share and analyze cyber threat information across sectors and with other sharing hubs to help protect Canada’s businesses, government, consumers and economic prosperity. Companies and government agencies leverage shared information and generate new analysis to make cyber attacks more difficult and costly—and to increase the likelihood that attackers will be apprehended.

Cyber attackers are no longer limited to traditional entry points like employee mobile devices and laptops. They are now attacking companies through every entity that interacts with their business systems, including customers, the supply chain and providers of business services.

Vulnerabilities are also being introduced as companies extend beyond their core businesses—for example, utilities and network companies selling through retail outlets or retailers offering financial services—using entirely new systems and processes.

On its own, no sector, no business or organization is safe from cyber attack. The best way to counter attacks is by sharing information and resources as widely as possible.

THAT’S WHY WE NEED YOU AND YOU NEED US.


For more information, please contact us at info@cctx.ca or 613-747-2283.

Name: Huron Geomatics Inc.
Description:
Established in 2002 by Douglas Culbert, Huron Geomatics is now leading the charge in high accuracy information and dynamic imagery for mapping, design/engineering, and inspection projects!

The vehicle mounted system can map/scan data at normal traffic speeds for roadway surface condition assessments, roadside feature inventories, and geographically correct 3-dimensional measurements.

The system includes a high-resolution LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) scanner oriented to cover the road surface and adjacent buildings up to 100 meters / 300 feet away. A high resolution digital camera captures 180 degrees forward facing images at fixed distance intervals (with 2 passes providing 360 degree imagery) All sensor inputs are recorded and time stamped to a common internal clock.

The data is post-processed and geo-referenced with the LIDAR to provide a 3D image representation which can then be exported to industry standard formats. The point cloud and image data can be integrated with standard applications (Autodesk/AutoCAD, ESRI/ArcGIS) to provide a foundation for extracting features, measuring, designing, and analyzing!

Name: Polar Data Catalogue (PDC)
Description:
The cryosphere - sea ice, lake ice, river ice, snow cover, permafrost, and glaciers - plays a significant role in the Earth's climate system. With respect to the cryosphere, Canada occupies a unique geographic position on the globe in that much of the planet's northern cryosphere falls within Canada's territorial boundaries. Under the current conditions of rapid climate change over northern high latitudes (Olsen et al., 2011; Vincent et al., 2011), Canada has an obligation to measure, model, and understand the complex relationships between the cryosphere and the Earth's climate system to provide accurate and timely information on cryospheric variability and change to the public and decision makers.

In meeting this obligation, the wealth of knowledge and data generated through polar research must be managed to ensure exchange and maximize accessibility of relevant data, especially from publicly-funded activities, and to leave a lasting legacy (Parsons et al., 2011; Pulsifer et al., 2013). The Canadian Cryospheric Information Network (CCIN) was developed in the mid-1990's to fulfill this need. Created through a collaborative partnership between departments of the Canadian Government (the Canadian Space Agency, Environment and Climate Change Canada, and Natural Resources Canada), Dr. Ellsworth LeDrew at the University of Waterloo, and the private sector (Noetix Research Inc. of Ottawa, Ontario), the main objectives of CCIN have been as follows:

                   - To provide a data and information management infrastructure for the Canadian cryospheric research 
                      community,
                   - To enhance public awareness and access to cryospheric information and related data, and
                   - To facilitate the exchange of information between researchers, northern communities, decision makers, 
                      and the public.

Seeing this as an opportunity, we quickly began the developent of the most detailed GPS road and land feature maps in Western Canada, and OilTrax was born, which grew and spread quickly across the industry.

Triweb Technologies has since continued its trend of viewing roadblocks as opportunities for innovation, and has developed many custom software utilities that have brought rogue ideas to reality. Selling ingredients or supplements into China? The paperwork is the hard part — and it's getting harder.

China's health supplement market is on track to top RMB 430 billion in 2025, growing 20%+ online. We've seen firsthand what one missed requirement costs. A single 15kg shipment we know of was held at customs for 47 days over one missing import permit — a preventable $70,000+ loss once the follow-on order fell through. That's the mistake Nurbell exists to prevent, on the China side.

What we do:

AI compliance screening, human-verified — every gap analysis and regulatory alert is checked by our own regulatory team before it reaches you, not raw AI output.

GACC/CIFER registration — full project management, application to approval.

Documentation, translated — your FDA, Health Canada, or EU certifications, repackaged into what China's customs and regulators actually require.

Who we work with: overseas ingredient producers ready to export into China, and supplement contract manufacturers with spare capacity looking to land Chinese buyers.

Built by a PhD food scientist with 7 years in China's health ingredient industry, and a CTO who built AI platforms at Alibaba and TCL. (We also help Chinese exporters meet overseas requirements, so we know both sides of the border.)

Financial disclosures, stock trades, voting records, lobbying contacts, committee roles, conflict-of-interest reviews. All of it is already public, and all of it is scattered across dozens of registries, each with its own format, its own search box and its own quirks. Technically available. Practically unreadable.

Enter a postal code, get your MP and MPP. Read their record in a minute, not an afternoon.

Two commitments:

Non-partisan. The scoring engine treats every party identically, and our grading methodology is public, so anyone can audit exactly how a grade is computed.

Free. Parliamentary accountability shouldn't sit behind a paywall.

The goal is simple: make government data so easy to read that "I didn't know" stops being a defence.

Name: Citescan.ai
Description:
cite/scan helps B2B brands measure and improve how they appear in AI-generated answers.
As search shifts from Google to ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, and Gemini, the question is no longer just "do you rank?" — it's "do you get cited?" AI engines don't return a list of links. They pick a source, summarize it, and move on. If your brand isn't in that answer, you're invisible to a growing share of buyers doing research.
cite/scan scores any URL across three dimensions:
Visibility — are AI models finding and surfacing your content when asked relevant questions?
Credibility — do models treat your brand as a trusted, authoritative source worth citing?
Technical — is your site structured in a way that AI crawlers can actually read and use?
These three scores roll up into a Discovery Readiness Index (DRI) — a single number that tells you where you stand, and a prioritized fix list that tells you what to do about it.
Built for marketers and founders who need to stay found as search rewrites itself.

University of Toronto Frequently Asked Questions and Answers (UTFAQ) is a registered Non-Profit Organization, born out of a student club at the University of Toronto. Our dedicated editorial team periodically updated a diverse selection of articles and shared authorized pieces from other student clubs to ensure comprehensive coverage of all aspects of university life. In parallel, our offline activities, such as orientations and tax declaration sessions, offered students direct engagement with valuable resources.

UTFAQ's impact over the years has been significant and quantifiable: We published 270+ articles on topics ranging from course introductions to survival guides for freshmen. Our website accumulated over 1,250,000 hits by 2020, with our most popular page reaching 76,659 hits. We hosted annual orientations, information sessions, and other activities. By 2019, our active membership had grown to 38 and continued to increase consistently.

In 2020, as our founders moved on from university life, and with UofT offering many similar services, we made the tough but necessary decision to discontinue UTFAQ. We are immensely proud of our contributions and the difference we made in the lives of students. While UTFAQ is no longer operational, we keep this page active as a testament to our shared history and dedication to aiding students. We will forever remember the positive impact we had and the rewarding experiences we enjoyed while helping students transition smoothly into their new university life and Canadian culture.

Name: The Alpine Review
Description:
The world around us seems as turbulent as it has ever been. Tremors across industry, across culture, across the environment, are profoundly reshaping everything we know. But it’s too easy to get caught up in the noise of now and miss what it will all mean when the urgency fades.

We started The Alpine Review a decade ago as an attempt to understand those tremors from a long-term point of view — to look at how our immediate moment is shaped by the past and will shape us in the future. The output of that process was a high-design, conceptually bold, ad-free and mammoth-sized print magazine which we called “a compendium of ideas for a world in transition”. After three successful issues, we thought the project had fulfilled its mission and it entered a happy, self-imposed hiatus in 2016.

Since then however, we’ve observed the development of a number of worrying dynamics which make our future seem ever more fragile and uncertain. Our intuition ten years ago was a world rebalancing. Now it seem humanity might be facing a more dramatic faith, unless we find a way to complete a massive redesign effort of our systems and institutions.

This is why we’ve decided it was time to bring back The Alpine Review for another tour of active duty. Step one was to create a digital home for the project, making all the existing content available for those who have followed us along in our journey and to newcomers who might not have come across the printed magazine before (in this case, welcome!). The second step will come later in 2022, when we determine what our role can and should be in our evolving information ecology.
